body_markdown:
Is there a more easily distinguished, classic American car than a 1948 through 1964 Cadillac? These cars set a standard, signifying our infatuation with tailfins, and are fondly remembered to this day.[But while Peak Fin occurred in 1959](https://www.hagerty.com/media/opinion/klockau-classics/1959-cadillac-eldorado-biarritz-dream-jet/) (as[Peak Brougham did, in your author’s opinion, in 1976](https://www.hagerty.com/media/opinion/klockau-classics/1976-cadillac-fleetwood-red-white-and-brougham/) ), there are compelling arguments that the slightly reduced fins and other mild styling updates for 1960 Cadillacs resulted in an even prettier car.


[Thomas Klockau](https://www.hagerty.com/media/author/tklockau/)


Like all the other full-size 1960 GM cars, the ’60 Caddys weren’t drastically different from the ’59s, but I personally think the 1960 Cadillacs are more elegant than the 1959s. Oh, sure, I love the ’59s, especially the Eldorado Biarritz[and hardtop Eldorado Seville](https://www.hagerty.com/media/opinion/klockau-classics/klockau-1959-cadillac-eldorado-seville/) .


Thomas Klockau


But I think a ’60 Sixty Special in Ebony Black—like today’s featured example, owned by friends Lauren Schweitzer Cody and Jonathan Cody—or perhaps in Glencoe Green or York Blue, would be even more elegant parked in front of, say, your author’s favorite supper club, The Cellar in Geneseo, than a 1959-equivalent model would be.


[Thomas Klockau](https://www.hagerty.com/media/author/tklockau/)


This car, like many others previously featured here, was seen by myself and fellow Cadillac fanatic Jayson Coombes at the 2022 Cadillac & La Salle Club (CLC) Grand National, held in Lombard, Illinois. Despite the early rain, we were not deterred, and Lauren’s Fleetwood was one of the first cars I zeroed in on (well, after I’d gawked over a Georgian Silver ’76 Fleetwood d’Elegance).


[Thomas Klockau](https://www.hagerty.com/media/author/tklockau/)


I had heard about this car and seen photos on Facebook, but this day was the first time I’d seen the car in person. It was gorgeous, even in the early rain.


Thomas Klockau


And while all 1960 Cadillacs had smaller fins than the previous 1959s, the fins were definitely not small. They were just a bit lower, with jet-pod taillights replaced by smooth, inset taillamps with a gentle curve to them. I love them.


Thomas Klockau


As always, the Fleetwood Sixty Special was largely considered the nicest “owner-driven” Cadillac, excepting the much longer and typically chauffeur-driven Series Seventy-Five Sedan and Limousine.


Thomas Klockau


The Sixty Special was only available as a six-window pillarless body style. Base price was $6233. Curb weight was 4880 pounds and 11,800 were built for the 1960 model year.


[Thomas Klockau](https://www.hagerty.com/media/author/tklockau/)


Like all Cadillacs, the Sixty Special was powered by a 390-cubic-inch V-8. Hydra-Matic automatic transmission was, of course, standard. Power was 325 hp at 4800 rpm.


[Thomas Klockau](https://www.hagerty.com/media/author/tklockau/)


Unless, of course, you opted for the extra-cost Eldorado engine. That consisted of the addition of three two-barrel carburetors, which bumped power to 345 hp. The standard 390 made do with a single four-barrel carb.


[Thomas Klockau](https://www.hagerty.com/media/author/tklockau/)


Of course, this was a Cadillac, so there were lots of standard features. This was no Chevy Biscayne! As the brochure enticed, “From the dark red cloisonne crest on the front fender to the nine louvers accented in chrome on the rear quarter panels, the Fleetwood Sixty Special will be recognized as a motor car of custom design and coachwork.


Thomas Klockau


“The Fleetwood is further distinguished by its handfitted, weather-resistant fabric roof cover in matched body tones. Ten elegant interior choices include: turquoise, gray, or Persian sand Clarion cloth with matching Florentine leather bolsters …


[Thomas Klockau](https://www.hagerty.com/media/author/tklockau/)


“Locarno blue, green or fawn Cardinal cloth with matching bolsters … black Cardinal cloth with white Florentine leather bolsters … gray, Locarno blue or sage tan wool broadcloth.”


[Thomas Klockau](https://www.hagerty.com/media/author/tklockau/)


And while I’d love to see one in dark blue or Persian Sand, there’s something to be said for Lauren and Jonathan’s car in black with the black and white interior. Elegant, but with a little bit of brightness with the white leather bolsters and white accents on the door panels and dash.


[Thomas Klockau](https://www.hagerty.com/media/author/tklockau/)


The few available options included air suspension (which your author would not have recommended; despite GM’s experience with air suspension on its buses, it was … problematic on passenger cars) for $215, Autronic Eye (an automatic headlamp dimmer) for $46, the Eldorado engine for $134.40, and fog lamps for $43.


[Thomas Klockau](https://www.hagerty.com/media/author/tklockau/)


No matter what color combination or options you may have selected, a Fleetwood Sixty Special made a statement in 1960: “I’ve made it.” And: “I may enjoy driving to supper clubs, drinking martinis, and playing golf.”


Thomas Klockau
